properties.label: Lévis / Lauzon, Lower Canada
properties.note: Abraham's birthplace (Lauzon seigneury, 1792); the family left Lower Canada in 1841 (Neill 1881; Find a Grave 50657843).

properties.label: Montreal
properties.note: Head of St. Lawrence steam navigation; every westbound route from Quebec passed through it (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Kingston
properties.note: Where St. Lawrence travel met the Lake Ontario steamers (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Buffalo
properties.note: Eastern terminus of the upper-lakes steamers to Detroit, Mackinac and Chicago (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Detroit
properties.note: Old French town and the first major call for lake steamers bound west (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Mackinac
properties.note: Straits station where the steamers turned south into Lake Michigan (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Chicago
properties.note: End of the lake voyage; the canal to the Illinois River did not open until 1848 (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Peru / La Salle, Illinois
properties.note: Head of steamboat navigation on the Illinois River in 1841 (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: St. Louis
properties.note: Neill: the family 'went to St. Louis by boat and spent the winter' of 1841-42 there.

properties.label: Galena
properties.note: Lead-mining port, the busiest upper-Mississippi call for St. Louis boats in the 1840s (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Prairie du Chien
properties.note: Fort Crawford and the mouth of the Wisconsin; a regular steamboat landing (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Fort Snelling / Mendota
properties.note: Head of steamboat navigation and the start of the cart trails north; Neill: 'they came via boat to St. Paul, then to Red River'.

properties.label: St. Paul
properties.note: Pig's Eye landing in 1841, St. Paul's chapel from 1841; the Red River carts ended here (Hess 1989).

properties.label: Traverse des Sioux
properties.note: Minnesota River crossing on the West Plains (Minnesota Valley) trail (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Lac qui Parle
properties.note: Fur post and mission on the upper Minnesota, on the West Plains trail (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Lake Traverse
properties.note: Head of the Red River drainage, where the trail left the Minnesota valley (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Pembina
properties.note: Métis settlement just south of the 49th parallel; junction of all three Red River trails; Kittson's post from 1844.

properties.label: St. Boniface / Red River Settlement
properties.note: Bishop Provencher's mission across the Red from Fort Garry; the family lived here 1841/42-1845; Rose Angélique married Alexander Ducharme here 26 Nov 1844 (Wall 1964).

properties.label: Old Crossing, Red Lake River
properties.note: The Woods Trail's ford of the Red Lake River near Huot (Gilman 1979) (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Detroit Lake
properties.note: The Woods Trail skirted its shore 'for nearly two miles' (Schultz 1894) (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Otter Tail Lake
properties.note: Where the Woods Trail turned east into the Leaf Hills toward the Mississippi (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Crow Wing
properties.note: Mississippi ford and trading village at the mouth of the Crow Wing River; the Woods Trail crossed here from 1844 (NRHP 90002201).

properties.label: Sauk Rapids
properties.note: Where the Woods and Middle trails met and ran down the east bank to St. Paul (reconstructed stop).

properties.label: Little Canada (Lake Gervais)
properties.note: Section 8 of New Canada: the family settled here in 1845; Abraham patented lots 1-2 on Lake Gervais in 1849 (Neill 1881; BLM GLO).
